project.title: Desktop Service Manager
project.summary: A desktop console for inspecting managed user services, issuing contract-aware lifecycle actions, and following scoped logs through Constellation.

preview.description: The March 2026 Tauri interface brought service controls, runtime properties, and live logs into one workspace.

blocks.body:
## Put service diagnosis in one workspace

Process Manager is an on-demand desktop console for user services managed by Constellation. Its current Tauri application combines a Rust backend with a React and TypeScript interface, bringing service state, controls, runtime properties, and journal output together.

The project evolved from a Python and GTK dashboard through the Tauri interface shown above. The maintained version organizes services in a sortable process list with stable status, PID, memory, and uptime columns, then opens the selected service’s controls and recent operations alongside it.

## Use the same service contracts as the rest of the system

Membership and metadata come from Constellation’s current user-service inventory projection. Available actions follow each service’s declared activation contract and run through the public Constellation CLI. On-demand services can be started and stopped without being offered an unsupported start-at-login setting.

Raw unit-file state remains visible, with linked installation distinguished from enabled startup. Archived packages and packages awaiting migration can still be inspected while their mutation controls remain unavailable.

## Separate observation from control

The backend gathers live state in one batched systemd observation and emits a complete snapshot when membership or runtime state changes. The frontend consumes those events and requests only incremental journal entries, avoiding a second competing service observer.

Per-unit action coordination keeps lifecycle requests attached to the correct service. Projection diagnostics and action receipts give the operator an explanation when discovery or an operation cannot complete.

## Keep investigation focused

The all-services journal view includes only discovered managed units. Service selection, severity filters, text search, and controlled scrolling help narrow the stream while retaining context.

Status-first ordering puts failed and indeterminate services near the top. At smaller window sizes the interface progressively hides lower-value columns before stacking the panes, preserving service names and state for as long as possible.
